goal: Set up CS61C lab tools on this Mac

page_concerns.concern: Asks you to run a script from the internet with curl and bash
Asks you to type a password-based copy command that changes your account

steps.title: Install Apple's command line tools
steps.explanation: This adds the developer tools that the lab needs. A window may pop up asking you to confirm.

steps.title: Check your Java version
steps.explanation: This shows whether Java is already installed. If nothing is installed, a pop-up may appear.

steps.title: Install Java 17 if needed
steps.explanation: Only do this if the Java check did not show version 16 or higher. Get the Adoptium OpenJDK 17 .pkg installer for Apple silicon (aarch64).

steps.title: Check your Python version
steps.explanation: This shows which Python version is installed. Version 3.6 or higher is needed.

steps.title: Check Python's security certificates
steps.explanation: This tests that Python can connect to secure websites. If nothing is printed, it is working.

steps.title: Fix certificates if an error shows
steps.explanation: If you see a certificate error, open the Python folder in Applications and run Install Certificates.command. Then open a new Terminal and run the check again.

steps.title: Install the campus VPN
steps.explanation: The VPN lets you reach the course computers from anywhere. Follow the bSecure Remote Access VPN instructions from the course page and make sure there are no errors.

steps.title: Sign up for your CS61C account
steps.explanation: Go to WebAccount and sign up for a CS61C instructional account. It may take a day or two before you can create it.
steps.click_target: Sign up for a cs61c instructional account on WebAccount

steps.title: Test a connection to a hive machine
steps.explanation: Replace cs61c-??? with your account username. Make sure the VPN is connected. You will be asked for your password, and nothing will show as you type.

steps.title: Create the SSH settings folder
steps.explanation: This makes a folder where your SSH shortcut settings will go. It is safe to run even if the folder exists.

steps.title: Add the SSH shortcut settings
steps.explanation: Open the file ~/.ssh/config in the vim editor. Paste the CS61C config from the course page and replace cs61c-??? with your username. Then save and quit.

steps.title: Test the shortcut connection
steps.explanation: This connects to hive7 using the shortcut you just set up. Type exit when you are done.

steps.title: Make a passwordless login key
steps.explanation: This prints or creates an SSH key on your account. The course page asks you to run it straight from the internet.
concerns: Downloads and runs a script from the internet without showing it first

steps.title: Copy your key to your account
steps.explanation: This copies your key to the course computer so you can log in without a password. It asks for your password.
concerns: Asks for your password and changes your account

steps.title: Test passwordless login
steps.explanation: You should connect to hive5 without being asked for a password. Type exit when you are done.

steps.title: Show your public key
steps.explanation: Open Terminal and print your public key. Replace path_to_ssh_key with the file location shown earlier and add .pub at the end.

steps.title: Add your key to GitHub
steps.explanation: In your browser, go to GitHub Settings, then SSH and GPG Keys, and add a new key with your public key. Give it a name that helps you remember it.

steps.title: Test the GitHub connection
steps.explanation: This checks that GitHub accepts your key. A success message shows your username.

steps.title: Finish the rest on the course computers
steps.explanation: The remaining Git exercises and the lab files run on the hive machines, so do them after an SSH login.

finish_check.message: CS61C hive shortcut settings are in place
